_doc: Revert-verify for ems__Bug 1fdfd7fb (ExoSync body merge kept a section TWICE when its heading was renamed differently on both sides), subject = StructuredMerger.ts, guard "Divergent-rename guard" in mergeBody. Axes H* in packages/core/tests/unit/services/sync/StructuredMerger.heading-rename.test.ts. H3 is a regression control no mutant locks: the guard takes no part in a one-sided rename. H7, H11 and H18 are the named prices: the guard counts ANY one-sided new heading (an added section, a one-sided rename, a level change), so a base section gone from both sides next to such an edit on each side conflicts - an unrelated delete-and-add (H7), the SAME rename plus an addition on each side (H11), the SAME rename plus a one-sided rename on each side (H18); they flip together with the fix. H22 locks that a NON-blank preamble takes part (its text would otherwise land twice). M6 (additions condition weakened to "either side added") is locked by H12-H15, H20 and H21. Note for ems__Bug 96a86732 (rename on one side vs delete on the other resurrects the section): at the level of heading keys H14/H15 (a convergent delete plus a one-sided addition) are the same input as rename-vs-delete, so ANY guard for that ticket that judges keys alone turns H14/H15 red - it has to look at section content, or H14/H15 must be re-judged as prices. No axis here asserts the resurrection either way. Known misses that belong to 96a86732, not here: a rename onto a heading the base already has (renumbering), and different headings put over the preamble text when a blank line follows the frontmatter - both still keep text twice. Incidental overlap, named: a rename-vs-delete where the DELETING side also added a section, and different headings put over the preamble text with no blank line after the frontmatter (H22), already conflict through this guard (the reason does not claim a rename). Run: python3 -I ~/.claude/bin/mutant-driver.py <this spec> after setting `tree` and `subject` to YOUR checkout.
subject: <ABSOLUTE PATH TO YOUR exocortex CHECKOUT>/packages/core/src/services/sync/StructuredMerger.ts

M1_guard_never_fires._note: The pre-fix behaviour. H7 and H11 redden too, as expected: they are the named prices of the guard.

M3a_local_convergent_addition_counts._note: A heading added on BOTH sides (the same rename) must not count as a local-only addition.

M3b_remote_convergent_addition_counts._note: Mirror of M3a on the remote side.

M6_either_side_added._note: The plain shape of a rename-vs-delete guard (ems__Bug 96a86732): it would quarantine merges that must stay merges.

M7_reason_swaps_sides._note: The reason reaches the user as `warn: quarantined <path>: <reason>` in `exosync sync` and in the plugin's warning log; naming the sides the wrong way round sends them to the wrong version.

M8_exactly_one_local_addition._note: H9 is the only axis where one side adds TWO keys (a new section next to the renamed one).

M11a_removed_on_remote_only._note: H5 locks the mirror (removed on local only); H19 is its mirror input.

M12a_local_base_key_counts_as_added._note: A base section the REMOTE side dropped while the local kept it is not a local addition.

M13_any_preamble_excluded._note: Type-preserving: the preamble test keeps its shape, only the blank-text half is made always true.
